A1.justification: Both readable 37-page PDFs describe the same V-JEPA 2.1 work and include Appendices A–D. Text and visual comparison establish that v1 genuinely omits the distillation table added in v3; this is not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original representation-learning experiments, downstream benchmark evaluations, robotic experiments, and component ablations in the main text and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a table reporting results for the already-described distilled models.

M1.justification: The dense predictive loss, deep self-supervision, modality-specific tokenizers, and distillation procedure are unchanged. Distilled ViT-L and ViT-B models were already described in v1 Section 2.3.6 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: All nine benchmarks in the added distillation table were already used in v1. The table adds model-specific results without introducing datasets, tasks, domains, or test scenarios.

E2.justification: External baseline membership is unchanged. Section 3.10 already compares distilled models with the ViT-G teacher and scratch-trained ViT-L; v3 Table 11 documents those same comparisons.

E3.justification: Training settings, model sizes, metrics, and evaluation protocols remain unchanged, including Appendices A–C. Both versions state that the distilled models follow the existing evaluation protocol; the added table does not establish changed settings or reruns.

E4.justification: Table 11 expands quantitative support for the existing distillation-versus-scratch analysis, including ViT-L K400 accuracy of 84.3 versus 86.9 and IN1K accuracy of 81.8 versus 84.9. The component, weighting, multi-layer, and resolution ablations otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The added table uses point estimates without introducing run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests. Existing statistical and averaging disclosures are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 11 adds previously unreported entries, including distilled ViT-L NYUv2 RMSE of 0.336 and distilled ViT-B SSv2 accuracy of 74.5 and DAVIS score of 67.0. Other entries repeat existing results: ViT-L distilled SSv2 accuracy of 76.5 and ADE20K mIoU of 46.7 already appeared in v1 Section 3.10. Existing tables retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and loss equations in Section 2 are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims. Effective distillation into compact models was already a claimed contribution; Table 11 adds support without changing its scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations, mechanism explanations, and limitations remain unchanged. The new table caption reiterates Section 3.10's existing interpretation that distillation improves smaller models and approaches teacher performance.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, distillation stages, evaluation instructions, and code-access information are unchanged. Model parameter counts displayed in Table 11 were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and research positioning are unchanged. Related-work text shifts across pages 23–24 to accommodate the added table.

P1.justification: Section 3.10's unresolved 'Table ??' reference becomes 'Table 11'; subsequent table references and the document date/version header are updated. The prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the four-row, nine-benchmark 'Benefits of Distillation' table on page 23, causing limited text reflow on pages 23–24. Appendix Tables 11–13 become Tables 12–14 without substantive display changes; figures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs an identifiable reporting omission: Section 3.10 now points to an actual table with fuller evidence for compact-model performance and distillation benefits. This improves completeness and makes the comparison easier to assess while leaving the central scientific content unchanged. The existing DAVIS inconsistency remains: Section 3.10 implies a teacher score of 67.0, whereas Tables 8 and 11 report 69.0.
